q: Which feature of ATP synthase lets the energy of proton flow be converted into chemical energy in ATP?
options: A rotor spins as H+ pass through, turning a stalk that reshapes the catalytic sites binding ADP + Pi
A gated channel opens only when ATP binds to it, letting electrons pass through into the matrix to O2
An active site uses reduced NAD as its substrate, transferring a phosphate group to ADP
A carrier protein exchanges ATP for O2 across the membrane each time a proton passes
explanation: ATP synthase is a molecular motor. Protons passing through the membrane-embedded part make it rotate; the attached stalk turns inside the catalytic head, cycling each active site through shapes that bind ADP + Pi, join them into ATP, then release the ATP. Roughly 3–4 H+ pass through for every ATP made.
